pages.text: This Coastal Planet A TIME-TRAVEL PLAYBOOK FOR INSPIRING COASTAL COMMUNITIES BY RUTH CATLOW AND ANN LIGHT This Coastal Planet works a little differently than most community visioning workshops. It is also not a typical role-playing game. As a facilitator, your role is to guide your group of 15–20 people on a 3-hour journey of imagination, conversation, and shared storytelling — helping them explore the past, present, and future of coastal/marine settlements they care about. Participants will step into the shoes of children and adults with a burning passion, moving through time and collaboratively creating answers to challenges ahead. The game is experiential, reflective, and collaborative. Connect across generations. Connect across distance. Connect with coastal and marine life.

Introducing The Four Workshop Stages The following script is designed to guide participants through a structured, staged journey. Pay close atten- tion to the suggested time allocations to maintain bal- ance, purpose and focus throughout the workshop. Approx 45 minutes Stage 1. Welcome, Introductions, The Interspecies Meditation and Sharing Circle The welcome sets a friendly tone and moves into a practice to sensitise participants to the lives of other species. Each player connects with a partner species. Approx 20 minutes Stage 2. Preparation for Play Participants are asked to add events from personal, global and partner species history to a 200-year time- line running back to 1875 and forward to 2075. 55 minutes Stage 3. The Play Participants move into role and participate in 3 scenes. With each scene-change characters age a generation or reincarnate, advocating for their beloved coastal settlement. 20 minutes Stage 4. De-role and Reflection De-roling gives participants a chance to step out of their characters and reflect on what they learned about their hopes for themselves, their community, and future generations.

Stage 1. Welcome 5 minutes Participants arrive and are welcomed at the door. Facilitator A stands near the entrance. Facilitator B arranges pebbles on the central table. Name labels are handed out at the welcome desk. Facilitator A Speaking to the room as people settle. Welcome everyone. We're so glad you're here. Today we're going to travel through time together — not as ourselves exactly, but as characters who care deeply about this coastline and everything that lives here.

"Before we begin, I want to name a few things about where we are and why we're gathered. [Name your location.] This place has a long relationship with the sea — with the creatures, the weather, the industries and communities that have shaped it over generations…" your version Facilitator B And I'm here to make sure we have everything we need along the way. Holds up the snack packet. Including, apparently, seaweed popcorn. Note The humour here is intentional. It eases tension at the start of the role-playing and models a dynamic of care between the two facilitators — making the play feel interesting rather than merely instrumental.

What You Need to Run the Workshop The Script Before hosting this event, you'll need to lightly add detail to the script to help your participants connect their priorities to their experience of coastal regions. Download Script Template. Timeline Poster You can either send this digital file to be printed approx. 840mm × 1680mm or create your own timeline poster using a roll of wall lining paper. Stationery Post-it notes and thick pens Character sheets (one per participant) Biros for each participant Name labels (two per participant: one for real name, one for character name) Furniture & Scene Props Chairs for all participants and facilitators Timeline poster displayed on a wall or large table 4 tables labelled "child", "young adult", "mature adult", and "elder" Pebbles: one per participant, palm-sized and pocket-friendly Refreshments Water, soft drinks, tea and coffee Sea-themed snacks like seaweed popcorn
